guarantees.claim: Six input sign signals are inverted before connection to the regular FSM: ctr_ready_i = ~ctr_ready_n, ctr_we_i = ~ctr_we_n, cipher_in_ready_i = ~cipher_in_ready_n, cipher_out_valid_i = ~cipher_out_valid_n, cipher_crypt_i = ~cipher_crypt_in_buf_n, cipher_dec_key_gen_i = ~cipher_dec_key_gen_in_buf_n.
The remaining inputs to u_aes_control_fsm (including ctrl_qe, op, mode, etc.) are connected directly without inversion.
All output ports of u_aes_control_fsm are connected to the corresponding module-level signals, including idle, output_valid, input_ready, and control updates such as ctrl_we, data_out_we, iv_we.
The aes_control_fsm instance is parameterized with .SecMasking(SecMasking).

assumptions.claim: Inputs ctr_ready_n, ctr_we_n, cipher_in_ready_n, cipher_out_valid_n, cipher_crypt_in_buf_n, cipher_dec_key_gen_in_buf_n must adhere to active-low convention (logic 0 = asserted).
assumptions.cond: when the AES control FSM is active
assumptions.risk: If any of these signals violates the active-low rule, the positive FSM will receive an inverted value (e.g., an asserted signal read as deasserted), leading to incorrect sequencing and potential security-sensitive data corruption.

assumptions.claim: The parameter SecMasking must be set consistently to enable or disable masking across the design.
assumptions.risk: If SecMasking does not match the actual masking datapath logic, masking may be partially disabled, leaking intermediate values.

assumptions.claim: rst_ni is an active-low asynchronous reset; it must be asserted (0) to initialize the FSM.
assumptions.risk: If rst_ni is not properly asserted, the FSM may start in an unknown state, potentially causing undefined output or secret leakage.

uncertain_points.claim: Comments state that outputs like data_out_we, data_in_prev_we, ctr_incr, cipher_in_valid, cipher_out_ready, cipher_crypt_out_buf, cipher_dec_key_gen_out_buf, key_init_we, and iv_we will be inverted later to produce their _n counterparts. The chunk does not contain this inversion; it must be implemented elsewhere in aes_control_fsm_n.
uncertain_points.cond: after this instantiation, in a lower part of the file
uncertain_points.risk: If the inversion logic is missing or incorrect, the negative-logic outputs driving the datapath may be stuck at the wrong polarity, causing functional failure or accidental clearing of sensitive data (e.g., data_out_clear_we might be inverted incorrectly, skipping a security wipe).

uncertain_points.claim: The SecMasking parameter is not checked locally; its value is passed unchanged to the FSM instance. It is unclear whether a mismatch between SecMasking and actual masking logic can be detected or safely handled.
uncertain_points.risk: Masking could be silently disabled or double-enabled, leading to side-channel leakage or functional deadlock in masked paths.
